title: A lock manager
hints: Keep per lock: owner, recursion count, an abandoned flag and a FIFO queue; and per process, the lock it is waiting for. Handing a lock to the next waiter happens in two places (release and death), so write it once.

For the deadlock check, start at the lock's owner and follow "which lock is this process waiting for, and who owns it" until the chain ends. If you arrive back at the requesting process, waiting would complete a cycle.
requirements: Recursive ownership and FIFO queues behave like Win32 mutexes with fair waiting.
Lock order is enforced for ranked locks.
Requests that would deadlock are refused instead of queued.
A dead process's locks pass on as abandoned, to waiters or to the next acquirer.
stretch: Turn it into a real service: a named pipe server (milestone 2) that runs a `LockManager`, with clients sending acquire and release requests, and the server watching each client's process handle so that a crashed client's locks are released as abandoned automatically.
